questions.skill: Use factored form to describe the graph of a polynomial function
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: p(x) = (x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 3). What are its zeros and its y-intercept?
questions.prompt_markup:
p(x) = (x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 3).
What are its zeros and its y-intercept?
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent form. All parts are required. p(0) = 2 · (-1) · (-3) = 6.

questions.skill: Use factored form to describe the graph of a polynomial function
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Describe the end behavior of y = x³ - 4x.
questions.prompt_markup: Describe the end behavior of y = x³ - 4x.
questions.correct_answer: As x increases without bound, y increases without bound; as x decreases without bound, y decreases without bound.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent wording (up to the right, down to the left). The leading term x³ decides.

questions.skill: Use factored form to describe the graph of a polynomial function
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Which describes the end behavior of y = -x³?
questions.prompt_markup: Which describes the end behavior of y = -x³?

choices.text: It rises to the left and falls to the right.
It falls to the left and rises to the right.

questions.correct_answer: It rises to the left and falls to the right.
questions.grading_note: For large positive x, -x³ is very negative; for large negative x, it is very positive.

questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Graph p(x) = (x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 3). Mark the zeros and the y-intercept, and show the end behavior. (Use the grid for x; the y-scale is up to you.)
questions.prompt_markup: Graph p(x) = (x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 3). Mark the zeros and the y-intercept, and show the end behavior. (Use the grid for x; the y-scale is up to you.)
questions.correct_answer: A curve crossing the x-axis at -2, 1, and 3, through (0, 6), falling to the left and rising to the right
